title: Recognizing Revenue
description: Determine whether revenue is recognized at a point in time or over time.
html:
Step 5 — Recognize revenue

Revenue is recognized when or as a company satisfies a performance obligation by transferring control of a promised good or service to the customer.

Two broad patterns

Point in Time

Revenue is recognized when control transfers at a particular point.

Over Time

Revenue is recognized progressively as the performance obligation is satisfied.

Point-in-time example

A retailer sells a television for $2,000.

The television is delivered and control transfers to the customer.

Revenue Recognized = $2,000

Over-time recognition

A performance obligation is recognized over time when the applicable criteria for over-time recognition are satisfied.

Examples of circumstances considered

  • The customer simultaneously receives and consumes benefits as the entity performs.
  • The entity's performance creates or enhances an asset that the customer controls as it is created.
  • The entity's performance creates an asset with no alternative use to the entity and the entity has an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date.

Simple service example

Assume a company provides a qualifying service evenly over 12 months for a total transaction price of $24,000.

Assume an appropriate measure of progress indicates that performance occurs evenly throughout the year.

$24,000 ÷ 12 = $2,000 per month

After three months:

$2,000 × 3 = $6,000 Revenue Recognized

What if over-time criteria are not met?

If a performance obligation does not qualify for recognition over time, it is satisfied at a point in time.

CPA thinking

Don't begin by asking: "When did the customer pay?"

Ask: "When did control of the promised good or service transfer?"

The entire five-step model

  1. Identify the contract.
  2. Identify performance obligations.
  3. Determine transaction price.
  4. Allocate transaction price.
  5. Recognize revenue when or as obligations are satisfied.

quiz.prompt: A company provides a qualifying 12-month service for $36,000, and an appropriate measure of progress shows the service is provided evenly. How much revenue is recognized after four months?
quiz.explanation: $36,000 ÷ 12 = $3,000 per month. After four months, $3,000 × 4 = $12,000 of revenue is recognized.

objectives: Explain recognizing revenue and its underlying principles.
